steps.what: Take to-go orders and clarify items, quantities and collection needs
Prepare to-go orders by checking and packing food for collection

tasks.design: Use the existing {OTHER} point-of-sale system to capture the order, then check and pack it physically. Keep clarification and preparation with the host; no new self-service channel is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Correct packing depends on the actual order and actual food.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing order capture already supports the handoff; its runtime earns no saving.
tasks.still_hard: Clarify substitutions and check that the collected package matches the guest's request.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve uncertainty with the guest and kitchen before packing.
tasks.altitude: Order-taking and preparation duties stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Check order completeness and communicate substitutions.

evidence.claim: Physical packing and guest clarification remain human work; existing digital order capture alone provides no new saving.

assumptions: Boundary is host order-taking and packing, excluding cooking and payment, which have separate unchanged owners.
OTHER is the existing point-of-sale system. The host captures item identifiers, quantities, requested changes and collection details in s1, including manual clarification time.
The kitchen produces food after receiving the order and before s2 in its existing cooking task. The host physically checks readiness and completeness in s2; no free ready flag is assumed.
Native order capture is sufficient; no new integration or upkeep is introduced, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Whether hosts pack all takeaway orders
research_questions: Which order discrepancies are found during physical packing?

already_counted.description: Host clarification, capture and packing remain fully counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and net=0 with no incremental work. No physical preparation time or existing system runtime is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Inform patrons of establishment specialties and features and answer questions

tasks.design: Keep the welcome and explanation with the host, using the existing menu in {DOCS} as a reference. Ask the kitchen or manager about uncertain availability or features rather than generating an answer.
tasks.previous_blocker: The useful explanation depends on the guest's question and current service conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing menu access supports the conversation without replacing it.
tasks.still_hard: Explain accurately and recognise questions that require kitchen confirmation.
tasks.human_edge: Read the guest's interest and provide a clear, personal explanation.
tasks.altitude: No change in service duties or decision rights.

reach.learn: Describe specialties accurately and escalate uncertain ingredient questions.

evidence.claim: Explaining restaurant features is direct guest service; a booking tool's capabilities do not establish savings for this conversation.

assumptions: Boundary is explanation, excluding reservations, order capture and food preparation.

The manager and kitchen provide current menu and service information through existing briefings before s1. The host asks about uncertain details during s1; no structured sold-out or dietary suitability flag is presumed.
Existing briefing work is unchanged and earns no saving. Native document access is enough; no new tool, data capture or upkeep is introduced, justifying zero incremental work.
unknowns: How hosts receive daily specialty updates
research_questions: Which guest questions require checking with the kitchen?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Existing briefing and guest conversation remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Receive patrons' dining reservations and capture requested date, time and party size
Check reservation time and party size against available table capacity
Record an available dining reservation in the reservation book
Explain reservation details and resolve unavailable or unusual requests

tasks.design: Configure the existing {OTHER} restaurant reservation system to check capacity and save ordinary requests atomically from the host's captured fields. Keep phone capture, guest explanation and unusual requests with the host; add no voice model or new guest data-entry requirement.
tasks.previous_blocker: A separate availability check and manual entry can duplicate information already gathered from the caller.
tasks.enabler_now: Reservation systems provide capacity-aware books and seating plans that can combine those operations.
tasks.still_hard: Special arrangements and disputed or unclear requests require conversation.
tasks.human_edge: Offer a useful alternative and negotiate arrangements outside configured limits.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate reservation handling; no new discretion over service capacity.

reach.learn: Understand turn times, table combinations and blocked capacity.

evidence.claim: Zenchef provides a booking widget and digital seating plan; TheFork Manager provides a reservation book and seating plans.
The host-captured capacity and recording design and savings are unmeasured model-knowledge scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary covers host-assisted reservation intake through guest explanation, excluding greeting, seating on arrival and meal service.

OTHER is a restaurant reservation system. The host captures date, local time, party size, guest name, contact channel and any non-sensitive special request in s1; all capture and correction time remains in its 40% share. Free text or incomplete fields remain manual.

The supervisor supplies opening hours, table identifiers, capacities, allowed combinations, turn times and blocked intervals before capacity checking. Existing capacity planning remains unchanged; additional setting verification is counted as 4 other-role hours per 100 focal baseline hours.

The reservation book supplies existing reservation identifiers, times, party sizes and table allocations from prior recorded bookings. s2 produces the capacity result; s3 rechecks availability and writes atomically to prevent concurrent double booking. Failed or ambiguous checks go to s4.
Test native configuration first. Savings apply only where a host currently checks capacity and re-enters a booking separately; an already automated book earns no new saving.
Focal upkeep is 8 hours per 100 baseline hours for configuration checks and additional exceptions; no guest or supplier labour transfer is assumed.
unknowns: Whether existing booking capture already checks and records atomically
research_questions: Can native booking configuration remove separate checking and re-entry while preserving phone service?

already_counted.description: Host capture, corrections, guest explanation and ordinary exceptions remain.

incremental.description: Check settings and investigate additional booking exceptions.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+0+0+20=60; gross=40, focal upkeep=8, central net=32. Conservative 8-20 assumes only part of separate checking and re-entry is removable and many unusual bookings stay manual; already integrated capture earns zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Operate cash registers for food and beverage payments

steps.what: Operate cash registers to verify bills and accept food and beverage payments

tasks.design: Keep payment acceptance in the existing {OTHER} point-of-sale system and payment terminal. The host verifies the bill, handles the guest interaction and resolves failed payments; existing total calculation is already automated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Payment arithmetic is already native system work, while guest interaction and cash handling remain physical.
tasks.enabler_now: No new configuration with demonstrated labour benefit is identified for this boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve disputed bills, tender changes and payment failures.
tasks.human_edge: Check the bill with the guest and handle payment exceptions responsibly.

reach.learn: Recognise payment failures and reconcile the bill before retrying.

evidence.claim: Existing register arithmetic is system runtime and cannot be counted again as newly saved host labour.

assumptions: Boundary is individual bill verification and payment acceptance, excluding order capture and end-of-day reconciliation.

OTHER is the existing point-of-sale system and terminal. Service staff create bill item identifiers, quantities and prices in the existing order workflow before this task; the host checks the bill and captures tender or cash during s1.
No new bill-matching flag or payment feed is assumed. Missing or disputed details are resolved manually during retained s1 time.
Native payment functions already operate; this unchanged design introduces no tool, transfer or upkeep, justifying zero incremental work.
unknowns: Payment methods and bill correction process
research_questions: Which exceptions consume host payment-handling time?

already_counted.description: Bill checking, payment acceptance and exceptions remain fully counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and net=0 with no incremental work. Existing register and terminal runtime earns no additional saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The host retains physical service and guest conversations while configured booking checks may reduce duplicate reservation handling.
reach: Help supervisors test reservation capacity settings.
role.ambitious_version: Spend available time helping guests with unusual booking needs, without expanding automatic service decisions.
